full_judgment: 2. Respondent Nos. 1-14 instituted the suit praying for declaration of their raiyati right to the disputed land measuring 29.82 described in the schedule to the plaint, plaintiffs case is that plaintiff No. 1 along with predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs 2-14 namely, Jabbar Ali Sheikh, Gagan Ali Sheikh, Hamid Ali Sheikh, Wahed Ali, Abdul Aziz Sheikh, Fajar Ali Sheikh, Sadaruddin Sheikh, Sirjan Ali Sheikh and Meser Ali Sheikh were recorded owners of the lands recorded in LR Khatian Nos. 370, 371 and 345 of Mouza Kapalbhera, PS Galachipa in the district of Patuakhali. Along the east of the said lands flowed the public navigable river Bura Gouranga. Due to diluvion some portion of the lands submerged in the river in 1347-48 BS and remained under water for 12/13 years and then again reformed in situ. The river then receded further towards cast and more lands accreted to the reformed lands. The plaintiffs possess the reformed lands as well as the accreted lands. Sometime in 1963 they applied to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) for their recognition as tenants in respect of the said lands under section 86 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The Additional Deputy Commissioner, referred the matter to the Local Circle Officer, (Rev) who claimed the suit lands as accretions to the Government lands and denied the plaintiffs' title to the same. Hence they claimed a total quantity of 29.82 acres of land. They denied that the Government had any possession therein.
